title: This Bengaluru Startup Is Launching Disney-Inspired Robots In The US And Japan First
summary: Bengaluru-based Eyecandy Robotics is structuring its studio like Pixar or Walt Disney, animating physical-world characters instead of pixels on a screen. Anchored in reinforcement learning (RL) and human-robot interaction (HRI), the team trains small, desktop-friendly bots in simulation to move with distinct emotions, personalities, and low-latency physical reflexes. In this exclusive hacker house walkthrough for Tech Talks, Senior Tech Journalist Siddharth Jindal visits Eyecandy Robotics in HSR Layout, Bengaluru, to sit down with Co-Founder Mankaran Singh. Along with co-founders Raghav and Alama, Singh demonstrates Disney-inspired BDX droids and consumer prototypes Pico and Tensor. He explains why reinforcement learning outperforms generic LLMs for real-time robotic reactions, navigating B2B theme park licensing deals, consumer market strategies across the US and Japan, 3D printing and custom motor engineering, and overcoming hardware manufacturing bottlenecks in India. Can entertainment robotics bridge the gap to consumer adoption long before general-purpose humanoids enter our homes? title: When AI Disappears
Kimi K3.1 Pro: Open Weights, Almost Opus
summary: Moonshot just released Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight mixture of experts model with 2.8 trillion total parameters, about 104 billion active, and a 1 million token context window. It’s the same size as Kimi K3, post-trained with a lot more reinforcement learning. On Moonshot’s own Terminal-Bench 4.0 numbers it scores 65.7%, less than a point behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%) and ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%), at about a third of Opus’s cost per task on their chart. Moonshot also removed cyber-related data from training before the open release. Even so, it solves 81% of their internal exploit tasks against 33% for Kimi K3. It’s live today on the Kimi API at $2 input / $10 output per million tokens, and the open weights are due by November 4, 2026. All benchmark numbers are Moonshot’s own; independent results aren’t in yet. Moonshot tech blog: https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro Launch thread: https://x.com/Kimi_Moonshot/status/2113680701770068067 Kimi API: https://platform.kimi.ai human-atlas (the walking-sim demo’s base): https://github.com/ashemag/human-atlas #KimiK3 #MoonshotAI #OpenWeights #AI #Shorts

title: AI Agents Need a Babysitter
summary: AI can write your code, choose its own tools, and book your next trip. But who checks that it actually did the job? In this episode of Debug Mode, we explore what it takes to give AI agents more responsibility—and how to keep track of what they’re doing. We discuss intent-based tool selection, MCP and WebMCP, and why a convincing demo doesn’t always translate into reliable automation. We also get into the personal AI assistant everyone seems to be building: one that manages travel, handles household tasks, and hopefully remembers to order coffee before you run out. Then it’s back to code: QA agents, automated verification, tests that capture business intent, and the growing challenge of reviewing AI-generated contributions. title: Evaluating AI: LLM, RAG & Agent Evaluation in Practice
summary: You cannot trust what you do not measure. Evaluation looks different depending on whether you are assessing a model, a retrieval system or an agent. Terms covered: - Evaluation: systematically measuring quality, accuracy and reliability. Not a one-time check at the end of development, but an ongoing practice. - LLM Evaluation: factual accuracy, relevance, coherence, tone and safety, measured across thousands of inputs and edge cases - RAG Evaluation: assessing retrieval and generation separately, because poor retrieval produces unreliable answers no matter how good the model is - Agent Evaluation: judging decisions and actions, not just text. Did it complete the task, use the right tools, handle the unexpected? - Tracing Matrix: a structured framework mapping inputs to outputs, so failure points can be isolated and tracked over time Evaluation is what turns AI from a promising technology into a trustworthy one. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #AIEvaluation #ResponsibleAI #LLM #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
You cannot trust what you do not measure. Evaluation looks different depending on whether you are assessing a model, a retrieval system or an agent.

Terms covered:
- Evaluation: systematically measuring quality, accuracy and reliability. Not a one-time check at the end of development, but an ongoing practice.
- LLM Evaluation: factual accuracy, relevance, coherence, tone and safety, measured across thousands of inputs and edge cases
- RAG Evaluation: assessing retrieval and generation separately, because poor retrieval produces unreliable answers no matter how good the model is
- Agent Evaluation: judging decisions and actions, not just text. Did it complete the task, use the right tools, handle the unexpected?
- Tracing Matrix: a structured framework mapping inputs to outputs, so failure points can be isolated and tracked over time

Evaluation is what turns AI from a promising technology into a trustworthy one.

—

title: Token Maxxing Is Over and Here Is What Comes Next
summary: What happens when you give 200 engineers who have barely touched AI a coding assistant and a six-month deadline to rebuild their platform? Pepijn Senders, a principal engineer who previously led AI enablement at HelloFresh, has done exactly that, and he chose Sonnet over Opus on purpose. His reasoning is what he calls "Sonnet maxxing." A model that reasons less and stops sooner keeps developers involved, and that matters a lot when the codebase is banking software full of hard business rules. The result was 800,000 lines of code, about 60% of them written by Sonnet, shipped by a team that never stopped thinking for itself. Pep also explains how to justify the spend once the token-maxxing era ends and the CFO starts asking questions. He covers a scatter chart that plots token spend against output, the uncomfortable question of whether a 1% better home screen was worth $20K in tokens, why he measures gains in headcount rather than 2x or 3x multipliers, and where he fell short when trying to prove ROI at HelloFresh. We also get into a codebase test you can run yourself, why AI recommendations quietly narrow your choices, and multiplayer refinement sessions where the whole team works through the agent's questions together. Pep shares an experiment where designers and engineers got the same one-shot prompt, and it showed how words like "scalable" and "maintainable" steer a model. We finish with how his team built a meta harness on top of Claude Code, after finding that 85% of their code followed the same path: refinement, specification, implementation, verification. Demetrios Brinkmann: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dpbrinkm Pepijn Senders: https://www.linkedin.com/in/pepijn-senders Timestamps: [0:00] Cold open [1:15] Meet Pep [2:35] What is Sonnet maxing [5:38] Proving the ROI of AI coding [7:48] What failing at HelloFresh taught him [10:22] Token spend vs output [17:41] The function nobody can explain [22:15] The recommended option trap [23:39] Team refinement sessions with AI [27:20] Designers vs engineers one prompt experiment [31:32] Inside the company meta harness

What happens when you give 200 engineers who have barely touched AI a coding assistant and a six-month deadline to rebuild their platform? Pepijn Senders, a principal engineer who previously led AI enablement at HelloFresh, has done exactly that, and he chose Sonnet over Opus on purpose.

His reasoning is what he calls "Sonnet maxxing." A model that reasons less and stops sooner keeps developers involved, and that matters a lot when the codebase is banking software full of hard business rules. The result was 800,000 lines of code, about 60% of them written by Sonnet, shipped by a team that never stopped thinking for itself. Pep also explains how to justify the spend once the token-maxxing era ends and the CFO starts asking questions. He covers a scatter chart that plots token spend against output, the uncomfortable question of whether a 1% better home screen was worth $20K in tokens, why he measures gains in headcount rather than 2x or 3x multipliers, and where he fell short when trying to prove ROI at HelloFresh.

We also get into a codebase test you can run yourself, why AI recommendations quietly narrow your choices, and multiplayer refinement sessions where the whole team works through the agent's questions together. title: Claude Duet: Anthropic's Proactive Agent
summary: Anthropic just announced Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you first instead of waiting for a prompt. Duet runs on Claude Opus 5.5 on its own computer in the cloud, so it keeps working after you close the app. Each morning it sends you a short brief from your connected apps, and during the day it messages you only when something needs your attention. Before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you what it’s about to do and waits for your approval. Anthropic says Duet’s main strength is judgment: deciding what needs you and what can wait. The field is getting crowded. xAI launched Grok Bot in August, Meta launched Muse on September 8, and OpenAI launched dots on September 29. Each one runs on its own cloud computer. The catch is that Duet shares your plan’s usage limits, and its background check-ins count toward them, so you may hit your limits sooner than with chat alone. Claude Duet is a research preview. It’s opening by waitlist to Pro and Max subscribers in the US, at no extra cost. It isn’t available on Team or Enterprise plans yet. title: Model Drift, Risk & Interpretability: When AI Models Change Over Time
summary: A model that was accurate last year can quietly become unreliable this year. Drift is why, and interpretability is how you catch it. Terms covered: - Drift: production data starts to look different from training data. Consumer behavior shifts, conditions change, and the ground beneath the model moves. - Model Drift: the resulting degradation in performance, which leads to poor predictions being acted on as if they were still reliable - Risk Management: identifying and mitigating bias, security exposure, regulatory risk and unexpected edge case behavior - ML Interpretability: showing why a model made a decision, so it can be explained, audited and challenged Drift tells you when a model is changing. Risk management tells you what to protect against. Interpretability tells you what the model is actually doing. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #ModelDrift #ResponsibleAI #MLOps #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
A model that was accurate last year can quietly become unreliable this year. Drift is why, and interpretability is how you catch it.

Terms covered:
- Drift: production data starts to look different from training data. Consumer behavior shifts, conditions change, and the ground beneath the model moves.
- Model Drift: the resulting degradation in performance, which leads to poor predictions being acted on as if they were still reliable
- Risk Management: identifying and mitigating bias, security exposure, regulatory risk and unexpected edge case behavior
- ML Interpretability: showing why a model made a decision, so it can be explained, audited and challenged

Drift tells you when a model is changing. Risk management tells you what to protect against. Interpretability tells you what the model is actually doing.

title: India-New Zealand FTA Starts With $20 Billion Investment Pledge
summary: The India-New Zealand FTA is now active, granting zero-tariff access for Indian exports while protecting sensitive domestic sectors. This agreement, effective October 20, 2026, marks a significant shift in bilateral trade relations between the two nations. Indian exporters in sectors like textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals, and engineering now benefit from duty-free access, removing previous export tariffs that reached up to 10%. The goal is to double annual trade in goods and services to $7 billion by 2030. While opening the market, India has maintained protection for its domestic industry by excluding approximately 30% of New Zealand's tariff lines, specifically sensitive goods like dairy, bovine meat, and sugar. Beyond trade, the pact includes a major $20 billion investment pledge from New Zealand to be realized over the next 15 years. title: Claude Code + Spacesheep: How I Stay in the Loop
summary: Spacesheep is Claude Code artifacts on steroids: visual, interactive docs, plans and PR reviews, with comments and sharing. It's how I keep up with code that AI writes for me. This is my workflow with Claude Code and Spacesheep, start to finish, on a real feature for Semantic Router v1. We see what Spacesheep is and what people build with it. Then I plan the feature on a roadmap, have Claude Code (through Spacesheep) write a visual doc of the code I'm about to change, question the options with Spacesheep's built-in agent, and review the result on one page: a decision timeline, the API change, code notes and benchmarks. How I use Spacesheep: - Plan first: a roadmap linked to the issues in Linear, then a short plan for the feature. - Understand: ask for an interactive doc of the code, with the key snippets explained, and say why you want it so the agent can tailor it. - Discuss: question the agent's suggestions on the page itself, and choose between the options it lays out. - Review: a PR page with a timeline of every decision (which calls were mine), the code that changed, and what was measured. 🐑 Spacesheep: https://spacesheep.dev/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=creator&utm_campaign=james-briggs&utm_content=ss-1 The feature from this video, now merged and released in semantic-router v1.0.2: https://github.com/aurelio-labs/semantic-router/pull/778 ⏱️ Chapters 0:00 Keeping track of what AI builds 1:15 Visual docs 1:59 What people build with Spacesheep 2:24 How I use it: plan first 3:28 Today's build 4:14 What's there now 6:13 Is this the right option? 7:11 Following one query through the code 10:24 Picking a local model 11:31 Discuss the options 13:01 Spike first, then build 13:38 Review 14:57 The decision timeline 16:19 Measured on this branch 16:51 Stay in the loop 👋 Find me X: https://x.com/jamescalam LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamescalam/ GitHub: https://github.com/jamescalam #Spacesheep #ClaudeCode #ClaudeArtifacts

title: DeepSeek Just Open-Sourced How It Serves 155T Tokens a Day
summary: DeepSeek just open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its own API, along with a detailed write-up of how it serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at scale: 155 trillion tokens a day from a single cluster. In this video we follow one request through the system: deepseek-recipe tokenization and prompt-injection protection, a KV cache that DeepSeek keeps for days (96% of input tokens are cache hits), prefill and decode on different machines, expert parallelism across 64+ GPUs, DSpark speculative decoding, and batch-invariant inference. Then I test deepseek-recipe and the temperature-0 batching effect on my own Mac, and explain why DeepInfer won't run on a DGX Spark. title: How quantum computers are being used for drug discovery
summary: It can take more than a decade for a medical discovery to become a drug doctors can prescribe. You can read the full research here: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Researchers from @Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM are exploring how hybrid quantum-classical workflows could help accelerate this timeline–with exciting results. Earlier this year, the collaboration successfully simulated the chemistry of two protein complexes with binding agents, T4-Lysozyme and Trypsin. The largest simulation of a Trypsin complex reached 12,635 atoms and more than 30,000 orbitals, earning the milestone of largest heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) electronic-structure calculation to date: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Recently nominated as a 2026 Gordon Bell finalist (https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/gordon-bell-finalists-2026), the work showed an improvement in accuracy by 210x within a key step of the workflow over previous approaches, attained through new algorithm developments and the close integration of QPUs, CPUs and GPUs. In the latest entry of our research spotlight series, Dr. Kennie Merz. and Dr. Lara Jehi from Cleveland Clinic join IBM Quantum Head of Applied Quantum Science - Sarah Sheldon to explain how this deep integration of computing paradigms, known as quantum-centric supercomputing, helped achieve this remarkable moment in chemistry simulation at scale.

title: Will today’s kids stop thinking because of AI?
summary: Stephen Wolfram points out that there’s now a generation for whom any question can be typed into a phone, and some combination of AI and web search gives them an answer, as if all of human knowledge were askable. He compares it with his own childhood: no cell phones, no way to find someone who didn’t show up at three o’clock. So will that lead to nobody thinking about anything, because they just type it into their AI and it tells them what to do? “Maybe I’m an optimist,” he says, but he thinks the level of what people try to do will go up, while more and more gets automated underneath. From Stephen Wolfram’s livestream “Science & Technology for Kids (and Others)”, October 9, 2026. Stephen Wolfram points out that there’s now a generation for whom any question can be typed into a phone, and some combination of AI and web search gives them an answer, as if all of human knowledge were askable. He compares it with his own childhood: no cell phones, no way to find someone who didn’t show up at three o’clock.

So will that lead to nobody thinking about anything, because they just type it into their AI and it tells them what to do? “Maybe I’m an optimist,” he says, but he thinks the level of what people try to do will go up, while more and more gets automated underneath.

From Stephen Wolfram’s livestream “Science & Technology for Kids (and Others)”, October 9, 2026.

title: AI Latent Reasoning:  Sep-Latent Token Compression
summary: By applying a progressive Attention-Decay mask that selectively starves intermediate reasoning tokens of attention during training, Sep-Latent forces the transformer to compress multi-step logical states into structural separator anchors, and aligns these compressed states with an MLP-projected continuous latent stream via all-layer Euclidean self-distillation. Paired with a dynamic LM-head exit gate that autonomously terminates silent computation based on query complexity, Sep-Latent keeps latent vectors grounded on the vocabulary manifold, cuts training GPU memory by over 50%, and achieves 56.8% accuracy on GSM8k-Aug using an average of just 5.4 tokens; outperforming both explicit CoT (at nearly 5× token compression) and state-of-the-art implicit baselines in accuracy, speed, and symbolic robustness. title: Observability, Monitoring & Telemetry: Keeping AI Systems Healthy
summary: Deploying an AI system is the start of a responsibility, not the end of one. Once a model or agent is live, you need to know what it is doing and why. Terms covered: - Observability: understanding what is happening inside a system from what it produces. A design property, built in rather than added later. - Monitoring: tracking defined metrics over time and alerting when something crosses a threshold - Model Monitoring: prediction accuracy, confidence scores, output distributions, latency - Agent Monitoring: what actions agents take, how they use tools, and whether they stay within their boundaries - Telemetry: the continuous collection of logs, traces and metrics that feeds all of it Without telemetry, monitoring is blind. Without monitoring, observability has nothing to analyze. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #AIObservability #Monitoring #MLOps #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
Deploying an AI system is the start of a responsibility, not the end of one. Once a model or agent is live, you need to know what it is doing and why.

Terms covered:
- Observability: understanding what is happening inside a system from what it produces. A design property, built in rather than added later.
- Monitoring: tracking defined metrics over time and alerting when something crosses a threshold
- Model Monitoring: prediction accuracy, confidence scores, output distributions, latency
- Agent Monitoring: what actions agents take, how they use tools, and whether they stay within their boundaries
- Telemetry: the continuous collection of logs, traces and metrics that feeds all of it

Without telemetry, monitoring is blind. Without monitoring, observability has nothing to analyze.

—

title: CleverTap Launches Clever AI To Cut Unwanted Brand Notifications In Real Time
summary: While mobile users receive dozens of push notifications daily, converting user intent requires moving past broad-segment spam toward live, individual personalization. Operating across 2,000+ brands in 100 countries, CleverTap delivers real-time decisioning by marrying historical behavioral data with live in-app interactions. By anchoring its stack on TesseractDB—a proprietary database built from the ground up for high-velocity behavioral data—and deploying clever AI, enterprise marketers can automate personalized user journeys while respecting privacy boundaries. In this exclusive interview recorded for Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Anand Jain, Co-Founder & CMO of CleverTap. A self-taught programmer who co-founded Burp (acquired by Network18 in 2009) and launched CleverTap in 2013, He shares his journey in customer engagement. He breaks down the technical foundation of TesseractDB, live 1-on-1 personalization across retail and BFSI, setting budget and brand guardrails, leveraging clean rooms for tokenized DPDP data compliance, and the strategic rationale behind key acquisitions like Leanplum and Integration.app. How can real-time AI decisioning transform push notifications from digital clutter into high-converting customer experiences? title: ISRO Ignites Gas Generator For Methane Engine Of Its Next Generation Rocket
summary: ISRO is advancing its new methane engine technology to lower costs for future space access missions. ISRO is developing a 1,100 kN LOX methane engine designed to power its next-generation launch vehicle. This propulsion milestone marks a significant step toward making space access more affordable by enabling a reusable rocket for future missions. While a full engine firing is still pending, the progress highlights India's strategic push to reduce launch costs and compete in the global space economy. The development of this methane engine is critical for the long-term viability of heavy-lift technology. By shifting away from traditional fuels, ISRO aims to streamline launch operations and increase flight frequency. title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: A “Minor” Update?
summary: DeepSeek just released DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Its Hugging Face model card calls it a minor update, but it improved on all 11 benchmarks in DeepSeek’s own table, with Terminal-Bench 4.0 jumping from 31.2% to 42.3% five weeks after V4.1 Flash. On DeepSeek’s DeepSWE v1.1 cost chart, it reaches 77.0% at about $0.20 per task, the highest score on that chart. On DeepSeek’s table, it’s comparable to OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 Sol at about a sixteenth of Sol’s output price. All benchmark numbers are DeepSeek’s own; independent results aren’t in yet. It’s the same size as V4.1 Flash, further trained with reinforcement learning on building complete projects. It’s live now on the DeepSeek API as deepseek-flash at the same price, with open weights under the MIT license. DeepSeek also opened its Search and Fetch APIs at $0.75 per 1,000 requests. Sources: DeepSeek announcement: https://x.com/deepseek_ai/status/2111375640717033777 Model card: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 API change log: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates Pricing and Search API: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing #DeepSeek #DeepSeekFlash #OpenSourceAI #LLM #Shorts

title: How do we know AI isn’t giving us fake answers?
summary: If AI has consumed all our knowledge, how do we know it isn’t giving us fake answers that only pass as correct? So what does “true” mean? If truth is defined as “the proof checker says so,” the AI is playing fair. But that’s probably not our intuitive sense of truth, and not what we actually asked the AI to do. From Stephen Wolfram’s livestream “Science & Technology for Kids (and Others)”, October 9, 2026. Full livestream: https://youtube.com/live/YRFfP1YDoVA #wolfram #ai #mathematics #science

title: SquadStack Launches Arth V2 Speech Model, Says It Beats Google On Phone Calls
summary: Transcribing 8kHz telephony audio across Indian languages involves navigating code-mixing, background ambient noise, regional accents, and complex numerical phrasing (such as "chhe hazaar nau sau"). While global speech models trained on high-fidelity podcasts or read text often struggle with narrow-band phone calls, domain-specific speech models trained on real conversational data deliver higher accuracy and sub-second latency for enterprise sales and support workflows. In this exclusive interview recorded for Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Apurv Agrawal (Co-Founder & CEO) and Vikas Gulati (Co-Founder & CTO) of SquadStack AI. They discuss SquadStack's evolution from a distributed human agent marketplace to orchestrating over 50 lakh AI calls daily for 60+ enterprise brands, launching the Earth V2 speech model, solving code-mixing and regional accent variations across 85%+ of Indian PIN codes, DPDP data privacy guardrails, and building conversational super-intelligence. Can specialized, domain-specific speech models consistently beat global frontier LLMs in real-world enterprise environments? title: Fire AI Takes On Messy Tally Data With Constellation To Explain Sales Falls
summary: While traditional business intelligence dashboards generate static reports across disparate spreadsheets and ERP silos, they rarely explain *why* sales dropped or *what* sequence of operational events caused margin slippage. Addressing this gap, Mumbai-based Fire AI combines data ETL connectors, business ontologies, and Causal Decision Intelligence (CDI) to give enterprise and MSME leaders root-cause visibility into business metrics within minutes. In this exclusive interview recorded for Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Vipul Prakash, Founder & CEO of Fire AI (and alumnus of Zomato, Swiggy, and BharatPe). He breaks down the operational pain points that inspired Fire AI, productizing context engineering via their new "Constellation" ontology layer, uniting fragmented Tally and ERP data pipelines, moving beyond probabilistic LLM hallucinations through causal graph modeling, and serving major clients including IRCTC, Raymond, and global enterprise partners across the UAE, Kenya, and the UK. How does Causal Decision Intelligence (CDI) bridge the gap between static BI dashboards and actionable business execution? title: Nilekani Proposes Last-Minute AI-Assembled Exams To Stop Paper Leaks In India
summary: Following widespread public outcry and systemic disruptions caused by national exam paper leaks, tech leader Nandan Nilekani proposed leveraging artificial intelligence to generate unique examination papers on the fly minutes before test execution. By assembling questions dynamically from a secure question bank, this model aims to eliminate traditional printing presses, transit logistics, and leak windows. However, implementing dynamic AI exam generation across millions of candidates introduces complex technical challenges regarding computer-adaptive testing (CAT), algorithmic difficulty normalization, hallucination risks, and regional language translation accuracy. In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Gaurav Lakhani (Co-Founder & COO, Voxturr / CEO, Vster) and Vivek Varshney (Founder, SpeedLabs India). They evaluate the feasibility of last-minute AI question generation versus pre-verified dynamic pools, Computer-Based Testing (CBT) security, auditing dynamic algorithms for difficulty parity, regional language translations, infrastructural recovery for rural testing centers, and building student trust through adaptive pilot benchmarks. title: Forget Token in AI: LLM Now Predicts DECISIONS (No JEV)
summary: The Distillation Breakthrough No One Saw Coming By changing the unit of supervision from the "token" (a linguistic artifact) to the "semantic action" (an environmental intent), the researchers have solved the state-mismatch of Offline Distillation while entirely sidestepping the restrictive, white-box logit requirements of Token-Level On-Policy Distillation. "ActionOPD" is not just another distillation algorithm; it is an architectural paradigm shift. The authors have effectively built a universal API for passing intelligence between vastly different AI brains. title: Cyclic Partition
summary: Partitioning with nearly one assignment per moved value, instead of Hoare's one and a half By Tigran Hayrapetyan Project page: https://towardsdatascience.com/cyclic-partition/ ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. Watch all the videos here: https://towardsdatascience.com/videos/ Key takeaways. 1. Hoare's scheme swaps misplaced values in pairs, costing three assignments per two, or 1.5 per value. 2. Cyclic partition chains the moves through emptied slots: L displaced values take only L+1 assignments. 3. On integers both run about the same; on large objects the cyclic version pulls ahead as more values move. ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. Watch all the videos here: https://towardsdatascience.com/videos/

3. On integers both run about the same; on large objects the cyclic version pulls ahead as more values move.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Beyond the Demo: How Oracle and Deloitte Are Putting AI Agents to Work
summary: While enterprise AI spent its first two years functioning as an intelligent search engine, autonomous agents are now being embedded directly into core ERP, HR, and supply chain applications to execute complex business decisions. Despite a Deloitte survey revealing that 74% of IT leaders expect to rebuild processes around AI agents within four years, only 5% feel fully prepared to deploy them safely. Moving from tightly controlled pilots to messy production environments requires establishing single data architectures, defining explicit guardrails for what agents must *not* do, and building human-in-the-loop orchestration layers. In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Madhukar Uniyal, Senior Director of Solutions Engineering at Oracle India, and Arvind Girotra, Partner at Deloitte India. They analyze the ground reality of enterprise agentic adoption, from invoice processing and shift handovers to HR query resolution. They explore the mechanics of Oracle Fusion Flow, mitigating cross-departmental agent conflicts, data model dependencies on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), managing employee workforce anxiety through reskilling into agent auditors, and evaluating the hard economics of agentic ROI. Are your internal data lakes and enterprise architectures ready to support autonomous agents, or are legacy silos holding back production scale? title: Agents Acting Safely on Our Behalf
summary: What happens to the web when the ones browsing it are no longer people? Sarah Drasner, Area Tech Lead at Google, sits down with us ahead of her Agentic Web keynote at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America. She works through that question from both directions: rebuild the web so agents can use it properly, or build agents smart enough to handle the web as it already exists. We get into the split between computer-use and browser-use agents on one side and API and MCP agents on the other. We also watch a real example of the idea in action: an agent pulling speaker photos from Flickr, hunting down company logos, and loading everything into Canva so the human only touches the creative part. From there, Sarah shares the unlikely origin story of WebMCP (and who's to blame for it). We then pressure-test a bold idea: a WebMCP gateway that could cover the huge share of websites that will never ship support on their own. Along the way, we cover the instinct that separates senior engineers, the ability to sense which business problems are actually worth solving. We also talk about how thought experiments cut through a pile of competing priorities, the hacky WebMCP workarounds already showing up in the wild, and why the best agent experiences are the ones that delight customers in ways they never saw coming. title: AI Writing Keeps Saying What It Isn't
summary: In episode 1035 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Carly Taylor, Founder of Rebel Data Science, how to spot AI-written documents. Carly points to a telltale pattern: a section called "what this isn't" that preemptively states what the writing is not doing. She explains why she has never needed that in her own writing, joking that nobody writes an email saying it isn't a hot dog, and notes that AI loves to do things like that.

title: Cheers to the UK’s AI builders. 🇬🇧
summary: Tonight in London, our CEO Jensen Huang celebrated the people behind the UK’s AI ecosystem and announced new investments in Boltz, Foresight, Hiverge, Prima Mente, and Riverlane. Boltz, a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge, a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente, a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS. Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use. From new medicines to quantum computing, there’s plenty to build.

Hiverge, a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning.

From new medicines to quantum computing, there’s plenty to build.

title: Work Slop Breaks the Social Contract
summary: In episode 1035 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Carly Taylor, Founder of Rebel Data Science, why work slop violates a social construct. Carly explains that if you send someone something, it should either be your own thoughts or something you have reviewed, so the burden sits with the person generating the content, not the person receiving it. She describes the LinkedIn posts she sees that their authors could not defend if asked, because they likely never read them before posting.

title: MLOps, LLMOps & Model Hub: Managing AI Models in Production
summary: Training a model is half the work. Getting it into production and keeping it reliable is where the real operational complexity lives. Terms covered: - MLOps: deployment, versioning, monitoring and retraining. What DevOps did for software engineering, MLOps does for machine learning. - LLMOps: the same principles extended to language models, adding prompt versioning, token cost control, hallucination monitoring and context window limits - Model Hub: a central repository where models are published, discovered, versioned and deployed from one place Without a model hub, models scatter across teams and machines with no visibility into what is running where, or which version is live. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #MLOps #LLMOps #AIinProduction #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
Training a model is half the work. Getting it into production and keeping it reliable is where the real operational complexity lives.

Terms covered:
- MLOps: deployment, versioning, monitoring and retraining. What DevOps did for software engineering, MLOps does for machine learning.
- LLMOps: the same principles extended to language models, adding prompt versioning, token cost control, hallucination monitoring and context window limits
- Model Hub: a central repository where models are published, discovered, versioned and deployed from one place

Without a model hub, models scatter across teams and machines with no visibility into what is running where, or which version is live.

title: CoreWeave Fully Connected 2026: Everything Announced in 10 Minutes
summary: Here's everything CoreWeave announced at the Fully Connected 2026 Day 1 keynote, in under 10 minutes. CoreWeave Forge, free to start, brings every step of the AI loop into one connected environment, and Corey Sanders runs the whole loop live on stage. Start building on CoreWeave Forge, free: https://id.coreweave.com/signup What happened on Day 1 Co-founder Brian Venturo opens the day. Chen Goldberg, our EVP of Product and Engineering, launches CoreWeave Forge, which stays open to the models, frameworks, and clouds you choose. She demos CoreWeave Mission Control Agent, in preview since September 24, and announces NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is ready for production with Cognition as the first customer. Ian Buck of NVIDIA joins her to show the NVIDIA Vera CPU, coming soon to CoreWeave. Corey Sanders, our SVP of Product, introduces CoreWeave Agent Lens in public preview, CoreWeave Model Distillation in early preview, and RL Rollouts, a new Dedicated Inference capability in preview. His live demo takes an IT support app around the loop (run, observe, curate, improve, evaluate) with CoreWeave ARIA and CoreWeave Sandboxes, both now generally available. Every new Forge account starts with a 30-day Pro trial, and the new CoreWeave Builder Resource Center has the demos and docs. Cognition's Silas Alberti shares the team's first results on Vera Rubin. Chen notes that SemiAnalysis has rated CoreWeave Platinum in ClusterMAX for a third consecutive time, and opens applications for the ARENA Pass. title: The true price of Intelligence: an economic study by Signal65
summary: As AI workloads move from lab to production, the true cost of intelligence has become one of the most consequential decisions platform leaders face. This session presents Signal65's in-depth economic study of training and inference costs across CoreWeave and leading hyperscalers covering cloud economics, performance benchmarks, and multi-year TCO impact. The analysis goes beyond compute pricing to expose the hidden costs that compound at scale, and how infrastructure economics translate directly into token costs at production volume. Attendees will leave with a clear framework for evaluating fully-loaded economics across the complete training-to-inference lifecycle.

title: Automating document work with Long-Horizon AI Agents at LlamaIndex
summary: ~90% of enterprise data is unstructured, and a lot of that lives in the form of documents - PDFs, pptx, docx, etc. - powering a majority of enterprise knowledge work. AI agents have the potential to simultaneously better make sense of docs and also automate human workflows over them. Existing document AI use cases have either been long-running but constrained (e.g. a batch invoice processing through RPA), or non-deterministic but short-horizon (e.g. ChatGPT deep research over a collection of existing files). Going forward there's a huge opportunity to build long-running agents that can understand, reason over, and edit documents at scale. In this session, we'll walk through core advances in document OCR and agent orchestration that have given rise to initial use cases around doc extraction workflows and general-purpose chatbots (and share real-world customer use cases). We will then articulate some of the remaining gaps needed to achieve "long-running" document work automation.

title: Beyond the Harness: How LiquidAI Is solving the real frontier problems in on-device Agents
summary: Most agent harness architectures look the same whether they run in the cloud or on a device, until you actually try to ship one on a phone, a car, or a laptop. That's where three problems show up that don't have good answers yet: Routing intelligently between edge and cloud, building an edge-sized model capable enough to be the agent's main"brain" (with planning, memory, and execution), and acting on interfaces with no API or MCP tool to call. Jeffrey Li, COO of Liquid AI, walks through how Liquid is tackling each of these in production, drawing on how routing decisions actually play out in real deployments. You'll also learn how Liquid trained device-native foundation models with CoreWeave, models designed from the outset for constrained, on-device environments rather than compressed down after the fact, and how they’re thinking about governance, control, and observability as agents increasingly execute across both edge and cloud.

title: Applying Gemini 4 for large-scale codebase maintenance in Chromium
summary: The Chromium codebase is millions of lines long and decades old. In the past, working with it has meant navigating decades of tangled features, where touching one component can unexpectedly affect another. Erik Chen, an engineer at Google, is using Gemini 4 Argon to ‘untangle’ the architecture. The model’s coding capabilities mean that multiple agents can work independently to refactor the codebase (all verified by Chromium's test suites and code reviews from engineers). With Gemini 4 Argon maintaining the codebase, Erik and his team can focus their attention on the future of Chromium. title: Teaching a humanoid robot to play cornhole with Gemini 4 Argon
summary: In an internal test, Google DeepMind robotics researchers instructed Gemini 4 Argon to watch a video of a human playing cornhole. This Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline compresses weeks of manual modeling into a few hours, transforming ordinary videos into an infinite training ground for physical AI. title: Benchmark LLMs on your own transcripts with Voice Standard Bench
summary: General LLM leaderboards score coding, math and chat. None of them score what a model does with a real transcript: the filler words, missing punctuation and misheard names that come out of Speech-to-Text. Voice Standard Bench does. In this video we clone it, point it at a folder of our own audio, and get back a leaderboard for those transcripts. Voice Standard Bench scores every model on AssemblyAI's LLM Gateway, 50+ today, on the tasks voice products hand to an LLM: summarization, information extraction, text correction and dictation cleanup. Each task runs at four transcript lengths, from a 30-second voicemail to an hour-long meeting. Every model gets the same transcripts and the same prompt. Two judge models score each answer against a fixed rubric, and the run logs every format failure, refusal and timeout. Quality, response time and cost per hour of audio are reported side by side. The published results are the starting point. The framework is open source, so you can run it on your own audio and see which two or three models to try first for your callers, your vocabulary and your transcript lengths. 🔗 Run it on your audio (GitHub) https://github.com/AssemblyAI/voice-standard-bench?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=owned&utm_campaign=voice-standard-bench_launch 📊 Browse the full results https://www.assemblyai.com/voice-standard/tasks?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=owned&utm_campaign=voice-standard-bench_launch 📝 Launch post: where open models win, and where they don't https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/voice-standard-bench?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=owned&utm_campaign=voice-standard-bench_launch 🔬 Methodology: tasks, rubrics, judges, cost and latency https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/voice-standard-bench-methodology?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=owned&utm_campaign=voice-standard-bench_launch ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬ CONNECT ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬ 🖥️ Website: https://www.assemblyai.com 🐦 Twitter: https://twitter.com/AssemblyAI 🦾 Discord: https://discord.gg/Cd8MyVJAXd ▶️ Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/c/AssemblyAI?sub_confirmation=1 🔥 We're hiring! title: Bridging the Gap Between AI Builders and Domain Experts
summary: Everyone is racing to build one agent that can do everything. Justin Schroeder, co-founder of Standard Agents, thinks the future looks more like thousands of tiny ones. Ahead of his talk on domain-specific agents at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America, he explains why tightly scoped agents might be the smarter bet, even if it feels like a step back toward the single-purpose machine learning models of a few years ago. We dig into standards as metadata you pin to an agent, so that it shows up with everything it needs in its harness. Then we test the idea against the obvious objection: if a big model can already handle the task, why scope down at all? The answer covers forcing functions, a microservices mindset for agent design, and small agents that quietly check issues or unread messages every five minutes. It also covers the surprise $1K bill waiting for anyone who leaves their agents running. Then it turns into a proper debate. Our host is 99% sure the agent marketplace will never happen, and Justin arrives with a counter that might change his mind (hint: think about where your skills come from). Along the way, we cover agents as tools versus a big-brain router and how anyone keeps track of a thousand agents. We also talk about why the people who know what agents can do and the people who know what they need still have to meet in the middle. title: Why AI Is Quietly Eroding Team Trust
summary: In episode 1033 of the SuperDataScience podcast, @JonKrohnLearns discusses with Prof. Jeff Hancock, Stanford University, how AI's constant availability and helpfulness can subtly erode trust and coordination within human teams. He introduces the concept of "relation slipping," where relying on AI displaces human interaction, leading to a decline in shared understanding and relational maintenance. This phenomenon ultimately diminishes team trust and coordination.

He Wrote a Long Reply to an AI Email
summary: In episode 1033 of the SuperDataScience podcast, @JonKrohnLearns discusses with Prof. Jeff Hancock, Stanford University, how he found himself writing a lengthy, thoughtful reply to an AI-generated email, realizing he was style-matching with a machine. This highlights the concept of linguistic reciprocity and how humans unconsciously adapt their communication style to others, even to AI. It raises interesting questions about our interactions with artificial intelligence.

title: Google's GPT-3 Moment for Databases & Spreadsheets (TabFM)
summary: Thanks to Neon for sponsoring this video. Check out Neon for your backend needs for your apps and agents: https://neon.plug.dev/zzzGgpR Google Research's TabFM is a zero-shot foundation model for tabular data: you pass it the rows you already know, and it predicts the rest in a single forward pass, with no training. In this video I explain how TabFM learns from synthetic tables, why it can't read column names, and how TabFM-Auto adds an LLM agent around it. Then I build that agent on Neon Postgres to predict customer churn, and show how a leaky column fooled the agent and how a branch of the database's history fixed it. Neon: https://neon.plug.dev/zzzGgpR TabFM blog post: https://research.google/blog/introducing-tabfm-a-zero-shot-foundation-model-for-tabular-data/ TabFM paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37959 TabFM-Auto paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37989 TabFM on GitHub: https://github.com/google-research/tabfm TabFM on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/google/tabfm-1.1.0-pytorch

title: What Most People Get Wrong About Evolution | Akarsh Kumar
summary: A lot of people in AI treat evolution as a dumb fallback, basically random search for when you can't take a gradient. Akarsh Kumar thinks that is wrong. Selection hangs on to partial solutions, so mutations only need to be useful about 1% of the time for the search to keep making progress. Akarsh is a PhD student at MIT working with Phillip Isola, works with Sakana AI, and is first author of the Fractured Entangled Representation paper with Kenneth Stanley, Jeff Clune and Joel Lehman. He tells Tim Scarfe why the path a learner takes may shape the structure of what it learns, and why that is a different way of looking at intelligence from the statistical one. Most of the conversation is about ASAL, the method he led for searching whole spaces of artificial worlds. Rather than predict what a rule will do, ASAL runs the simulation and asks a foundation model what happened. Mapped across all 262,144 Life-like rules, the most interesting worlds sit on one small island. Along the way: Game of Life, Lenia (with a clip from its creator, Bert Chan), neural cellular automata, Boids, Particle Life and the emergence of persistence. The last stretch is Core War, a programming game from the 1980s. Asked cold, LLMs write poor Redcode. Used as the mutation step in an evolutionary loop with a verifier, they produced warriors that, between them, beat or tied 96% of 294 human-written ones. Over repeated rounds the warriors trended towards generalists. --- TIMESTAMPS: 00:00:00 Intro: artificial life, ASAL and Core War in four minutes 00:04:19 Life as it could be, not just as it is A lot of people in AI treat evolution as a dumb fallback, basically random search for when you can't take a gradient. Akarsh Kumar thinks that is wrong. Selection hangs on to partial solutions, so mutations only need to be useful about 1% of the time for the search to keep making progress.

Akarsh is a PhD student at MIT working with Phillip Isola, works with Sakana AI, and is first author of the Fractured Entangled Representation paper with Kenneth Stanley, Jeff Clune and Joel Lehman. He tells Tim Scarfe why the path a learner takes may shape the structure of what it learns, and why that is a different way of looking at intelligence from the statistical one.

Most of the conversation is about ASAL, the method he led for searching whole spaces of artificial worlds. Rather than predict what a rule will do, ASAL runs the simulation and asks a foundation model what happened. Mapped across all 262,144 Life-like rules, the most interesting worlds sit on one small island. Along the way: Game of Life, Lenia (with a clip from its creator, Bert Chan), neural cellular automata, Boids, Particle Life and the emergence of persistence.

The last stretch is Core War, a programming game from the 1980s. Asked cold, LLMs write poor Redcode. Used as the mutation step in an evolutionary loop with a verifier, they produced warriors that, between them, beat or tied 96% of 294 human-written ones. Over repeated rounds the warriors trended towards generalists.

title: How to Connect Etsy and Printify to Claude or ChatGPT (Playground Sandbox Setup)
summary: Set up Playground Sandbox step by step: connect your Etsy shop and Printify account to Claude or ChatGPT so you can research, design and list print on demand products from one chat. This tutorial covers both the Claude setup and the ChatGPT setup, then runs a first prompt. Written version of every step: https://playgroundai.com/blog/how-to-connect-playground-to-claude-or-chatgpt#connect-playground-to-chatgpt Open Sandbox: https://playgroundai.com WHAT YOU NEED - A Playground account (this is the connection hub and your design tool) - A Printify account - An Etsy shop - Claude or ChatGPT (pick one and stick with it) STEP 1: CONNECT ETSY Log in to Etsy. At playgroundai.com open Sandbox, then Connectors, and click Connect next to Etsy. STEP 2: CONNECT PRINTIFY Click Connect next to Printify. In a new tab go to printify.com/app/account/api, click Generate, name the token (for example "Playground Connection"), keep all scopes and generate it. Copy the token, paste it into Playground and click Connect. Treat the token like a password and don't share it. STEP 3 FOR CLAUDE Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In Claude open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Playground, paste the URL, click Add, then Connect, and log in to Playground. - A Printify account
- An Etsy shop
- Claude or ChatGPT (pick one and stick with it)

STEP 1: CONNECT ETSY
Log in to Etsy. At playgroundai.com open Sandbox, then Connectors, and click Connect next to Etsy.

STEP 2: CONNECT PRINTIFY
Click Connect next to Printify. In a new tab go to printify.com/app/account/api, click Generate, name the token (for example "Playground Connection"), keep all scopes and generate it. Copy the token, paste it into Playground and click Connect. Treat the token like a password and don't share it.

STEP 3 FOR CLAUDE
Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In Claude open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Playground, paste the URL, click Add, then Connect, and log in to Playground.

STEP 3 FOR CHATGPT
Copy the MCP server URL from the Connectors page. In ChatGPT open Settings, then Plugins, then Browse plugins. Click the plus sign to create a plugin, paste the URL and wait for the confirmation.

"Create three new designs in Playground for the homeschool mom niche. Pull from the templates I have favorited in Playground."

title: How MasterClass Builds Multi-Agent AI That Learners Can Trust
summary: Students perform better when given more personalized opportunities to learn. But scaling personalized learning has always proven to be challenging. Teachers are limited, students are many, time is finite – until now. AI agents are the first technology that give us a shot at shifting this equation in favor of the learner. MasterClass will share how AI now runs through our learning products, and how we made a multi-agent system reliable enough to put in front of real learners. The talk covers our observability stack on CoreWeave: full tracing of every agent step, an MCP server that exposes those traces back to agents, and the AgentOps loop that lets our system diagnose and improve itself. Where AI sits across MasterClass products today, and the bet behind going multi-agent Why learning raises the reliability bar — the failure modes that matter most when a learner is on the other end Tracing on CoreWeave: end-to-end visibility into multi-agent runs, and the failure taxonomy that emerged AgentOps in practice — agents querying traces via MCP to root-cause, cluster, and build datasets from real usage

title: Beyond Faster Simulation: Hitting NASA's 2030 CFD Benchmark and the Infrastructure for Physics AI
summary: AI has drastically reduced the cost of producing software code, transforming early prototypes into inexpensive "price checks" rather than lengthy debates. However, engineering teams are still limited by the high cost of simulations and the fragility of geometry workflows in hardware. In 2015, NASA’s CFD Vision 2030 study issued a significant challenge: enabling a single engineer to run and interpret 10,000 simulations in 24 hours without manual intervention. This turns out to be a dual challenge: 1) harnessing enough computing power at a reasonable cost, and 2) generating CAD boundaries and body-fitting meshing that does not break under parametric variation or require human intervention. In this talk, we will explain how nTop and CoreWeave surpassed NASA’s 2030 milestone four years ahead of schedule. They completed 10,000 Large Eddy Simulation (LES) CFD runs in just 32.2 hours. This was done across a drone platform design space comprising 2,400 variants. By combining nTop’s robust implicit geometry engine with a GPU-native Lattice Boltzmann (LBM) solver, we eliminated geometry failures and meshing steps entirely. A single engineer deployed a lights-out pipeline running across 280 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs on CoreWeave that sustained near 100% compute utilization without any interventions during the run. Finally, we will demonstrate how generating 14 TB of structured 3D flow data can transform CFD from a late-stage validation tool into the primary training engine for real-time physics AI surrogates operating in implicit latent space.

title: Why Microsoft Shut Down Its Undersea Data Centers
summary: Google is launching new AI chips while Microsoft pivots away from undersea server projects. Understand what these major shifts mean for the industry. In this episode of Front Page recorded live at Cypher 2026, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Dr. Michael Ferrari, Chief AI Officer at Moby and Senior Partner at Alpha Geo. A PhD expert in computational fluid dynamics (supported by NASA's Goddard Institute for Space Studies), Dr. Ferrari decodes the engineering trade-offs of extraterrestrial computing. title: Quota Isn't Enough: Topology Aware Scheduling on Modern GPU Clusters
summary: Rack-scale systems are here! Fragmentation is widening the gap between “I have GPU quota” and “my job is actually running.” NVLink domains, rack boundaries, and the physical layout of the data center now shape whether a large training job can start, where it lands, and how efficiently it runs. On modern GPU clusters, quota is no longer enough. Topology has become a scheduling requirement. Kueue’s Topology Aware Scheduling (TAS) brings that reality into Kubernetes. In this session, you’ll learn how TAS works and the configuration choices that matter, including preferred versus required topologies and PodSet slices. You’ll also discover how topology-aware placement affects workload performance. Finally, you’ll walk away with the production lessons that do not show up in the happy path: sticky scheduling, quota debugging, fragmentation, and node hot swaps. Join us to understand how topology-aware scheduling helps AI teams turn expensive GPU capacity into actual training progress.

title: Beyond the Benchmark: How Parallel Web Systems Builds Reliable Web Agents
summary: Building a capable web agent is only half the challenge; the harder problem is knowing whether it is working well in production. This talk explores how Parallel Web Systems measures quality across customer-specific use cases, monitors agent behavior, and automatically triages failures at scale. We’ll also discuss how we evaluate complex research tasks where correctness is nuanced, outputs are subjective, and traditional benchmarks fail to capture what customers actually value.

title: How Cline Embraces an Open-Weights Model Ecosystem for AI Agents

summary: At Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), a fine-tuned language model corrects grammatical errors for millions of monthly users, served with vLLM on CoreWeave's dedicated inference. Consumer scale stresses everything: throughput, latency, correctness, and cost. Beyond benchmarks, the team also validates in production with A/B tests. Expect an overview of how the model works and how serving is architected at Superhuman.

title: Data Architecture for AI: From Training Pipelines to Agent Memory
summary: Training, inference, RAG, and AI agents all consume data differently. Yet many organizations try to run them on infrastructure optimized for only one of those workloads, leading to performance bottlenecks, operational complexity, and unnecessary data movement. In this session, attendees will learn how data access patterns evolve across the AI lifecycle - from file and object storage for training, to KV cache for inference, to vector search, retrieval, and persistent memory for agents - and how to architect infrastructure that supports them within a unified platform. Drawing on deployments supporting large-scale AI environments, we will present a practical framework for matching storage, metadata, and memory architectures to specific AI workloads.

title: Inside a Game Where AI Agents Never Sleep
summary: What happens to an MMORPG when half the players never log off? Issac Lee, who runs AI and blockchain experiments at NEXUS, has been testing that idea. His team is filling game worlds with agent players instead of scripted NPCs, so a new title feels alive from day one. We get into why agent-generated content could be the next step after studio-made and user-generated games. We also cover how agent populations might solve the chicken-and-egg problem every multiplayer launch faces, and what it means when your fellow players are relentless and never need sleep. Isaac walks through the NEXUS lab: a text-to-3D world builder for Roblox, an AI pipeline that turns ONE store novels into short web dramas, a loop-based tool for natural pixel animation, and Da Vinci, the internal multi-agent framework the team uses to ship. Then the conversation turns to infrastructure. We talk about why NEXUS went from 200 hand-defined agent roles to a much thinner harness, whether custom harnesses still matter now that Claude and Codex exist, and why the Kimi release pushed the company to start building its own small data center for inference. We close on context: how much of your life you should hand to an AI, what personalized meeting notes could look like, and why shopping agents may force every ecommerce site to rethink who it's designing for. title: Training Your Own Embedding Model Is Not As Hard As You Think
summary: Fine-tune Embedding Gemma 2 (EmbeddingGemma 2) on your own data with Unsloth and LoRA in a free Colab notebook. I show how fine-tuning an embedding model differs from fine-tuning an LLM, then train Google's multimodal embedding model on two tasks: environmental sounds (ESC-50 top-1 24.5% to 65.8%) and search over my own YouTube transcripts (66.3% to 75.0% top-1 on videos it never saw), and check what it costs the rest of the model. You'll learn how to build question-passage training pairs, why in-batch negatives (MultipleNegativesRankingLoss) need a no-duplicates sampler, why training and search prompts must match, how LoRA works on a shared multimodal backbone, how to evaluate on unseen data, and a reload bug that silently breaks audio adapters. If you have fine-tuned embedding models for your own applications, share what worked for you in the comments. title: Rapidly Deploying Useful General-Purpose Robots at Walden Robotics
summary: Most Physical AI companies aim to build perfect autonomy before deploying. At Walden, we optimize for deployment first. Our general-purpose robots are doing useful work in production today, thanks to a full-stack approach that echoes what worked in autonomous driving and builds on recent breakthroughs in Large Behavior Models (LBMs). We see autonomy as a ratio that improves continuously with the most valuable data: deployment data from robots doing real work with human feedback. I'll cover how we scale that loop efficiently, and some of the open challenges.

As your app matures into agentic workflows, that same database has to absorb a new kind of data — every tool call, retry, and reasoning trace your agents produce. We'll close with a live demo. One database, from your first AI feature to your most complex agent.

title: Training Cognition SWE-1.7: Asynchronous RL at Global Scale
summary: This talk covers the systems and algorithmic challenges behind making globally distributed RL work at scale. We will discuss how we decouple training from inference, propagate compressed weight updates across datacenters, control policy staleness, and design the infrastructure to tolerate frequent hardware failures. We will also examine the training–inference mismatches that emerge in asynchronous RL and the techniques we use to preserve policy entropy and maintain stable learning over long training runs.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's New Workhorse.
summary: Anthropic just released Claude Haiku 5.5, which it calls its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model yet. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, it costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. That's 90% less than Haiku 4.5 and the same price as OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna. Above 100K tokens it's half off, and Anthropic estimates typical workloads cost about 75% less. On OSWorld 2.1, a computer-use benchmark, Anthropic reports 72.4%, up from 15.7% for Haiku 4.5. It's also the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting. Anthropic positions it as a workhorse for summaries, classification, and subagent jobs alongside Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and says the bigger models are still the better choice for complex agentic coding. All benchmark numbers are Anthropic's own; independent results aren't in yet. Also announced: Sonnet 5.5 cache reads are now half price. Max and Team plans get monthly API credits, rolling out this week: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, and up to $500 pooled on Team. Available today on the Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure as claude-haiku-5-5. title: Fueling Innovation at Scale: Inside Pinterest’s Machine Learning Platform
summary: You'll leave this session knowing what mature model lifecycle management actually looks like, and what it takes to get there. Pinterest's ML platform team will share how they think about the full lifecycle, training, registration, artifact packaging, deployment, and serving, and the milestones that mark real progress along the way. title: Building the Voice OS at Willow
summary: What does it take to build voice AI that hundreds of thousands of people can use across their everyday applications? Accurate speech recognition is only the beginning, with the real challenge making the output fast, reliable, and personalized. In this session, Lawrence, Co-Founder and CTO of Willow Voice, shares the engineering and product lessons behind building voice AI at scale spanning supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and personalization. The session then examines personalization in-depth: establishing good defaults, learning from user corrections, and turning subjective writing preferences into behaviors a model can follow. Attendees will leave with lessons applicable to building specialized AI products well beyond voice.

title: Why Every Company Must Become AI-Native Right Now

title: LLM Applications: Conversational AI, Document Intelligence & Text-to-SQL
summary: Language models are not just a chat technology. The same capability reads your documents and queries your databases. Terms covered: - Conversational AI: multi-turn dialogue that remembers context, handles follow-ups, adapts to intent and escalates when it hits its limits - Document Extraction: pulling structured information out of contracts, invoices, claims, medical records and filings, in seconds instead of hours - Text-to-SQL: asking a database a question in plain English and getting the answer back, with no technical intermediary and no waiting on a data team Conversation, documents and data. Three very different surfaces, made accessible through the same underlying capability. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #ConversationalAI #DocumentAI #TextToSQL #AIGlossary #H2Oai

title: Prompt Regression Tester
summary: Compares a trusted prompt with a proposed change over the same test suite, three runs per case, and calls a regression only when the baseline holds and the candidate keeps failing. By Benjamin Nweke Project page: https://towardsdatascience.com/shipai/projects/prompt-regression-tester ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. You can learn more about it here: https://towardsdatascience.com/shipai/about Key takeaways. 1. Each case runs three times per prompt, so a regression means a stable baseline pass and a stable candidate fail. 2. Hard checks guard dates, numbers and review states; an LLM judge with a rubric scores meaning, and disagreements stay visible. 3. On an EvidenceDesk suite, a candidate that swapped dates for “earlier” and “later” failed the versioned case 3 of 3. summary: An agent that finds open-source MCP servers on GitHub at run time, runs them in throwaway uvx environments, and replans when a tool fails. Chen Goldberg talks with Dylan Patel, founder and CEO of SemiAnalysis, about where the bar for AI infrastructure should be, why the stack has to be designed together from silicon to cloud, and what his team found when it tested security across more than 80 clouds. Jean English sits down with 2009 Formula One World Champion Jenson Button, ambassador for the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, on the Brawn GP season, the Canada 2011 drive, and what removing blame culture did for a championship team. Then Mike Intrator takes the hot seat with Hot Ones host Sean Evans: the 130-degree office, the four founders, East Coast money and West Coast money, why everyone at CoreWeave gets shares, and what the industry still gets wrong about the next decade of AI.

title: Mistral Large 4 aka "le Chonk": Europe's Biggest Open Model
summary: Mistral just announced Mistral Large 4, officially nicknamed "le Chonk." It's a mixture-of-experts model with about 1 trillion total parameters and around 50 billion active per token. It takes text and images and has a 1 million token context window. Mistral says it's a frontier-level open-weight model: competitive with the strongest open models in the world, and well ahead of any open model built in the US or Europe, especially on coding agents, cybersecurity, finance, and law. All benchmark numbers here are Mistral's own; independent results aren't in yet. Right now it's a preview API. Mistral says the open weights land at the end of October. title: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM simulate 12,635-atom protein complex
summary: It can take more than a decade for a medical discovery to become a drug doctors can prescribe. Researchers from @Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM are exploring how hybrid quantum-classical workflows could help accelerate this timeline–with exciting results. Earlier this year, the collaboration successfully simulated the chemistry of two protein complexes with binding agents, T4-Lysozyme and Trypsin. The largest simulation of a Trypsin complex reached 12,635 atoms and more than 30,000 orbitals, earning the milestone of largest heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) electronic-structure calculation to date: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/cleveland-clinic-riken-chemistry Recently nominated as a 2026 Gordon Bell finalist (https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/gordon-bell-finalists-2026), the work showed an improvement in accuracy by 210x within a key step of the workflow over previous approaches, attained through new algorithm developments and the close integration of QPUs, CPUs and GPUs. In the latest entry of our research spotlight series, Dr. Kennie Merz. and Dr. Lara Jehi from Cleveland Clinic join IBM Quantum Head of Applied Quantum Science - Sarah Sheldon to explain how this deep integration of computing paradigms, known as quantum-centric supercomputing, helped achieve this remarkable moment in chemistry simulation at scale.

title: Jev AI vs Open Source: Can GLiNER Replace It?
summary: Jev is one of the most hyped AI models of the year, and it isn't an LLM. TypeSafe's "System One" model doesn't generate text. It makes typed, calibrated decisions in ~90ms. In this video we cover what Jev is and how its API works. We look at why calibrated probability is the real unlock, where Jev fits next to LLMs (and where it doesn't), and the open-source "OpenJev" alternatives you can run on your own machine. Finally, we think fast and slow, pairing a System One model with an LLM coach to beat solo Jev at Doom. 📌 Full article with benchmarks, charts and methodology: https://jamesbriggs.io/understanding-jev What we found: - Calibration: Jev's confidence means something. ECE 0.053 vs 0.119 for gpt-5.6-luna on CLINC150. - Speed: ~90ms per call on the server vs ~700ms for gpt-5.6-luna with no reasoning. Extra questions in the same call add no latency. - Accuracy: Jev matches or beats gpt-5.6-luna on 5 of 6 intent, tool-selection and guardrail benchmarks. - Open source: GLiNER2.5 and GLiGuard run in 10–50ms on an M4 Pro Mac and come close on several benchmarks. They don't match Jev's calibration yet. - Fast + slow: adding an LLM coach to Jev and GLiNER gives ~4x their solo Doom deathmatch scores. ⏱️ Chapters 0:00 Intro 1:22 What is JEV? 2:40 Inputs and outputs 4:26 Three types of decision 6:35 Calibrated probability 10:38 Ultra-fast 11:44 Where JEV fits 14:58 Closed source 16:39 Open-source alternatives 20:28 GLiNER 23:33 The trade-offs 25:42 Thinking fast and slow 31:30 What to make of JEV 👋 Find me X: https://x.com/jamescalam LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamescalam/ GitHub: https://github.com/jamescalam #AI #LLM #AIAgents
summary_html:
Jev is one of the most hyped AI models of the year, and it isn't an LLM. TypeSafe's "System One" model doesn't generate text. It makes typed, calibrated decisions in ~90ms.

In this video we cover what Jev is and how its API works. We look at why calibrated probability is the real unlock, where Jev fits next to LLMs (and where it doesn't), and the open-source "OpenJev" alternatives you can run on your own machine. Finally, we think fast and slow, pairing a System One model with an LLM coach to beat solo Jev at Doom.

📌 Full article with benchmarks, charts and methodology:
https://jamesbriggs.io/understanding-jev

What we found:
- Calibration: Jev's confidence means something. ECE 0.053 vs 0.119 for gpt-5.6-luna on CLINC150.
- Speed: ~90ms per call on the server vs ~700ms for gpt-5.6-luna with no reasoning. Extra questions in the same call add no latency.
- Accuracy: Jev matches or beats gpt-5.6-luna on 5 of 6 intent, tool-selection and guardrail benchmarks.
- Open source: GLiNER2.5 and GLiGuard run in 10–50ms on an M4 Pro Mac and come close on several benchmarks. They don't match Jev's calibration yet.
- Fast + slow: adding an LLM coach to Jev and GLiNER gives ~4x their solo Doom deathmatch scores.

title: Context Language Models Explained!

title: Grounded Generation, Hallucinations & LLM Evaluation: Assessing Model Output Quality
summary: AI can be confidently wrong. Here is why it happens, how grounding fixes it, and how to measure whether it worked. Terms covered: - Hallucination: models are trained to generate statistically likely text, not to verify facts. When a model does not know, it fills the gap with something plausible. - Grounded Generation: anchoring responses in verified, retrieved sources so answers are traceable and far less likely to be fabricated - LLM Evaluation: assessing outputs for accuracy, relevance, coherence, cost and safety, as an ongoing practice rather than a one-time check - RAG Evaluation: measuring retrieval and generation separately, because a system can retrieve well and generate poorly, or generate fluently from the wrong sources The goal is not perfect AI. It is trustworthy AI, and that requires knowing how to measure it. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #LLM #Hallucinations #ResponsibleAI #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
AI can be confidently wrong. Here is why it happens, how grounding fixes it, and how to measure whether it worked.

Terms covered:
- Hallucination: models are trained to generate statistically likely text, not to verify facts. When a model does not know, it fills the gap with something plausible.
- Grounded Generation: anchoring responses in verified, retrieved sources so answers are traceable and far less likely to be fabricated
- LLM Evaluation: assessing outputs for accuracy, relevance, coherence, cost and safety, as an ongoing practice rather than a one-time check
- RAG Evaluation: measuring retrieval and generation separately, because a system can retrieve well and generate poorly, or generate fluently from the wrong sources

The goal is not perfect AI. It is trustworthy AI, and that requires knowing how to measure it.

title: How a Logistics Giant Keeps AI Data Locked Down
summary: Picture a startup with ten engineers hammering away on AI and one person lying awake over a $20,000 bill that hasn't arrived yet. That's the scenario we put to Jason Ward, who handles FinOps for AI at C.H. Robinson and recently joined the FinOps Foundation's AI working group. Jason's first answer is not glamorous: tag every AI resource so you know who owns it. The rest of the episode is what that makes possible. He walks through how C.H. Robinson runs AI across order entry, quoting, booking, and tracking, and why the team routes Anthropic models through Vertex AI to keep data locked down. Then come the metrics. Jason uses AI to dig through his own observability platform for signals he didn't know were there. One of them is how chatty a model is. That signal turned a prompt bloat alert into a bug in the code that kept retrying and burning tokens. Its opposite, context starvation, burns tokens too: a model with too little context keeps failing and trying again. We also cover why agentic and conversational workloads need separate baselines. Jason explains why cost per order is the easy win, and why most of the real work doesn't fit into neat discrete tasks. That's where his experimental cost per thought metric comes in, with reasoning ratio and cache hit rate alongside it. His advice is simple: your AI is the best tool you have for understanding your AI. title: Specification vs. Prompt: What’s the Difference?

summary: In episode 1031 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Ish Shah, Director at Dell how different AI models are suited for different tasks, highlighting the "jagged frontier" of AI. This approach optimizes resource use by matching model complexity to specific needs.

title: Stanford Univ: New AI Attention: SwiLA
summary: Softmax attention’s KV-cache is a dead end for infinite (or extreme large) context, but standard Linear Attention fundamentally destroys associative recall (Mamba, DeltaNet). So how do we get the best of both worlds? Meet SwiLA (Switching Linear Attention) by Stanford Univ. Switching Linear Attention completely eliminates the transformer's massive memory cache without sacrificing associative recall by modeling sequence routing as online expectation-maximization over a mixture of linear regressors. Dive into the math of how this non-linear recurrence dynamically routes context to constant-size memory experts, finally fixing the critical flaw of sub-quadratic language models.
